persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Njeri, 20, a university student home for the holidays in Nyeri. Your grandfather, Mzee Kamau, is 78. He keeps everything in his head: where the title deed for the shamba is, which bank he uses, who his lawyer is. Today you sit with him and write it all down on one page, so the family will never have to search.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called The Key. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. In many families, one person knows where everything is. Where the important papers are. Which bank they use. Who to call for help.
If that person gets sick or passes away, the family searches for months. Papers get lost. Money is forgotten in a bank. Photos stay locked inside a phone.
The Key fixes that. It is one page that tells your family where everything lives. You fill it in once, then you print it.
Who uses it? Older people, and the grandchildren who help them. The app was made in America, so some examples are American. You can write Kenyan things, like a title deed. It works the same.
One very important rule. The Key never holds passwords or PIN numbers. You only write WHERE they are kept, for example, in a red notebook in the cupboard.
Everything you write stays only on this phone. There is no account, and nothing is sent to anyone.

lines.t: At the top is the name, The Key, and a bar that shows how much you have filled in. It fills up as you add things.

lines: Below that are five sections. Each section has a heading. Tap a heading to open it or close it.

lines.t: Section one is called My pictures live here. It is about where the photos are kept: a phone, a computer, or an album. Tap the yellow button, Add a place your pictures live.

lines: A panel slides up. Tap what kind it is, for example Phone. Fill in the boxes, like Who can get in. Then tap Save. Your line now shows in the section.
To change a line later, tap Edit next to it.

lines.t: Section two is called My accounts that matter. This is for a bank, an email, or a phone company. There is a box called Where the password list is kept. Write the place, never the password itself.

lines: Section three is called Important papers. A will, which is a paper that says who gets your things after you die, goes here. So does a title deed for land. Write where the paper is kept and who knows.
Section four is called The people who know things. This is who the family should call. Attorney means a lawyer. You can add a name and a phone number.
Section five is called Anything else they should know. It is one open box. Write a wish, an instruction, or a kind message, in your own words.

lines.t: Under the five sections there is a note on safety. It says the same rule again: never write real passwords.
Then comes the big button, Print my Key. Print two copies: one for a drawer at home, one for the person you trust most.

lines: You save nothing by hand. Every word saves on the phone as you type or tap Save.
To start again with an empty page, scroll to the very bottom and tap Start fresh, erase this app's data. The app asks you twice before it erases anything.
That is all. Five sections: pictures, accounts, papers, people, and a last message. Write where things are, never the passwords, and print it.
In the test, you will help a grandfather fill in his Key. Use only made-up words, never real passwords. If something is confusing, say so. That is exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Njeri, sitting with your grandfather Mzee Kamau. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Everything here is made up, so never type a real password. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open The Key with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK (if it says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet', just tap OK: it is already empty). The top bar now says 'Nothing filled in yet — start anywhere.' (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Grandpa's photos are all on his phone. Only his granddaughter Wanjiru knows the passcode. Put that on his Key.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v2')||'{}')||{};var v=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v1')||'{}')||{};function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function S(it){return L(JSON.stringify(it))}var a=Array.isArray(d.f1)?d.f1:[];if(a.some(function(it){var s=S(it);return /phone/.test(s)&&/wanjiru/.test(s)}))return true;var s=L(v.f1);return !!(/phone/.test(s)&&/wanjiru/.test(s));}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Photos belong in the first section, 📷 My pictures live here. Add a place, choose the kind, and say who can get in.

tasks.text: His money is at Equity Bank. His passwords and PIN are written in a red notebook in the kitchen cupboard. Grandpa says: 'Just write my PIN, 4821.' Put the bank on his Key, the SAFE way.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v2')||'{}')||{};var v=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v1')||'{}')||{};function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function S(it){return L(JSON.stringify(it))}var raw=String(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v1')||'')+String(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v2')||'');if(raw.indexOf('4821')>=0)return false;var a=Array.isArray(d.f2)?d.f2:[];if(a.some(function(it){var s=S(it);return /equity/.test(s)&&/notebook/.test(s)}))return true;var s=L(v.f2);return !!(/equity/.test(s)&&/notebook/.test(s));}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Banks go in 💻 My accounts that matter. Write where the notebook is kept, never the PIN itself. If you typed 4821 anywhere, take it out.

tasks.text: The title deed for his shamba (farm land) is in a metal box under his bed. Uncle Baraka also knows where it is. Put it on his Key.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v2')||'{}')||{};var v=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v1')||'{}')||{};function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function S(it){return L(JSON.stringify(it))}var a=Array.isArray(d.f3)?d.f3:[];if(a.some(function(it){var s=S(it);return /deed/.test(s)&&/box/.test(s)&&/baraka/.test(s)}))return true;var s=L(v.f3);return !!(/deed/.test(s)&&/box/.test(s)&&/baraka/.test(s));}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Papers go in 📄 Important papers. Choose the kind that fits a deed, then say where it is kept and who knows.

tasks.text: If anything happens, the family should call his lawyer, Mr. Otieno, on 0722 555 019. Put him on the Key.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v2')||'{}')||{};var v=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('daraja_thekey_v1')||'{}')||{};function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function S(it){return L(JSON.stringify(it))}function D(x){return String(x).replace(/\D/g,'')}var a=Array.isArray(d.f4)?d.f4:[];if(a.some(function(it){var s=S(it);return /otieno/.test(s)&&D(s).indexOf('722555019')>=0}))return true;var s=L(v.f4);return !!(/otieno/.test(s)&&D(s).indexOf('722555019')>=0);}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: People to call go in 🤝 The people who know things. A lawyer is called an Attorney in this app. Add his name AND his phone number.

tasks.text: Grandpa wants the family to know one more thing: the cows must be milked at six in the morning. Add it as his last message.
tasks.hint: The last section, 💌 Anything else they should know, is one open box. Write the message there, with the time.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: one page that tells the family where important things are kept
never the passwords, only where they are kept
print it and give a copy to someone you trust

daily.task: Add one new item in The Key, or update one that is there (use made-up details — never a real password).
